memo_quote: Open science is a good public investment and a hard private one.
neutral_replacement: Open practices can create public and private value; investability depends on the product, appropriation strategy, entry price and financing needs.
reason: The packet does not estimate public benefit-cost ratios or the private return distribution for physical-science spin-outs.

memo_quote: Openness gives away what such investors usually pay for: patents, exclusive data, protected designs.
neutral_replacement: Disclosure before filing can forfeit some patent claims, and public release removes exclusivity over released data or designs. Other assets and properly retained rights may remain investable.
reason: Open source, open publications, open data and patent abandonment are different choices.

memo_quote: The customers who most want open tools are the ones with the least money.
neutral_replacement: Some academic buyers are budget-constrained; measure willingness to pay and repeat demand separately for academic, industrial and government customers.
reason: No customer-level willingness-to-pay or segmentation evidence is supplied.

memo_quote: A public funder (DOE's Genesis Mission, ONR, NSF) wants the opposite of what the venture investor wants.
neutral_replacement: Public funders and investors may both value reliable, adoptable technology, while differing on access, exclusivity and timing. Check each award and sponsor agreement.
reason: Public agencies are not interchangeable; industry sponsors are not the same persona as public funders.

memo_quote: That gap is mostly the timing of the listings: with listing-year controls it disappears.
neutral_replacement: The selected sample has a negative unadjusted median gap; a listing-year-adjusted log-relative-wealth model has a positive but imprecise coefficient. This does not establish why the gap arose.
reason: Changed estimand, sparse overlap and nonrandom listings preclude a causal timing explanation.

memo_quote: Openness hands the core to competitors and customers.
neutral_replacement: Public release lets others reuse the released layer, subject to its licence; the effect on capture depends on complementary assets, customer demand and governance.
reason: Assumes that the released layer is the commercial core and ignores adoption benefits.

memo_quote: Open lab tools sell mainly to academic labs.
neutral_replacement: The revenue mix of this proposed product is unknown; validate academic and industrial demand separately.
reason: Neither the kit nor one purchasing lab establishes the market mix for all open tools.

memo_quote: Publishing first forfeits the patents that unlock financing
neutral_replacement: Non-confidential enabling disclosure before filing can destroy novelty for affected claims; patent grants can help financing, but are not a prerequisite for every business.
reason: Title treats all publication as enabling disclosure and overgeneralizes a patent-applicant study.

memo_quote: Openness doesn't fix hardware economics; it removes the protection
neutral_replacement: Open hardware retains manufacturing, quality, brand and distribution barriers but can reduce design exclusivity and cloning costs.
reason: Implied loss of all protection is false.

memo_quote: Opentrons closed its hardware to scale
neutral_replacement: Opentrons expanded while its product openness changed; the packet does not establish that closing hardware caused scale.
reason: Temporal association is not a causal result; historical and current products differ.

memo_quote: If open source were a better model, it would show in returns.
neutral_replacement: A stronger operating model need not earn higher post-listing returns if its advantages are already priced at entry.
reason: Investment returns depend on price and risk, not just product quality or licence.

memo_quote: Licences are unstable, and closing later rarely pays
neutral_replacement: Some vendors changed licences and prompted forks; the evidence supplied does not identify the causal financial effect of relicensing.
reason: No frequency denominator or adequate counterfactual for rarely pays.

memo_quote: AI moves the value of open work to whoever runs the model
neutral_replacement: AI can shift costs and bargaining power away from maintainers, while also increasing usage, contributions, sponsorship and acquisitions. The net effect is business-model-specific.
reason: The memo itself contains counterexamples and gives no aggregate net estimate.

memo_quote: venture money only for the closed product.
neutral_replacement: Use venture funding only where the proposed business can produce venture-scale risk-adjusted returns, whether the monetized layer is open, proprietary or mixed.
reason: Software examples in the memo itself contradict a closed-only condition.

memo_quote: Destroys the asset
neutral_replacement: Pre-filing enabling disclosure can remove patentability for affected inventions; publication does not necessarily eliminate know-how, capability, trademarks or previously filed rights.
reason: Conflates one legal asset with the entire company.

memo_quote: Helps adoption, hurts capture, unless the hosted layer stays closed.
neutral_replacement: Open interfaces may aid adoption; capture can come from hosted execution, integrations, support, brand or reliability, without a demonstrated need to close the hosted code.
reason: The restrictive condition is not established by this sample.

memo_quote: For DOE's Genesis Mission or ONR, openness is a requirement, not a risk.
neutral_replacement: Check the applicable award: access obligations can coexist with IP, security, export-control and commercialization requirements.
reason: No award terms are supplied. A DOI alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for openness.

memo_quote: Strateos (folded 2023)
neutral_replacement: Strateos (pivoted from hosted access toward customer-site cloud-lab implementations in 2023).
reason: The company press release describes a pivot, not company closure.

memo_quote: At scale, open-source companies look like everyone else.
neutral_replacement: The small surviving sample has broadly comparable reported margins; it does not establish population equivalence or causation.
reason: Unmatched survivor cross-section and inconsistent JFrog treatment.

memo_quote: Openness isn't a structural margin penalty once there is a hosted product.
neutral_replacement: The snapshot does not establish whether openness causes a margin penalty or benefit for hosted products.
reason: A descriptive snapshot cannot rule out a structural effect.

memo_quote: Supabase's growth comes from agents choosing an open default.
neutral_replacement: Supabase reports strong growth and that more than 60% of new databases are launched by AI tools; the contribution of its licence relative to price, integrations and product quality is not identified.
reason: Reported correlation, not evidence that openness caused growth.

memo_quote: Open methods and full provenance, failed runs included, make a discovery more credible. That can shorten a customer's own validation, which is a genuine argument for openness.
neutral_replacement: Open methods and provenance can make results easier to audit and reproduce; any reduction in customer validation time remains to be demonstrated.
reason: Plausible mechanism, not measured qualification-time evidence.

memo_quote: For a public funder, openness is the return.
neutral_replacement: Access and spillovers are possible public returns; assess scientific quality, reproducibility, uptake, cost, security and maintenance as well.
reason: Access is an input or intermediate outcome, not a complete public-value metric.
